newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy forecast shows Commission doubts - economists.
newsitem.headline: Italy forecast shows Commission doubts - economists.

text.p: Economists said on Wednesday that the EU Commission forecast of Italy's deficit to GDP at 3.2 percent for 1997 showed that the Commission had reservations about Italy's financial performance and financial markets were likely to react adversely.
"The fact that Italy is above the three percent level suggests that the Commission has reservations about Italy's fiscal performance," said economist Ken Wattret at Paribas in London.
Economists said that the diplomatic pressure to push down Italy's deficit/GDP figure for 1997 had clearly failed, and that only emphasised the Commission's doubts on Italy.

Rome daily La Repubblica said earlier on Wednesday that the Commission was set to forecast the ratio of deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) at 3.1 percent for 1997 close to the three percent target set by the Maastricht target on European Economic and Monetary Union, scheduled to start in 1999.

In the Commission's forecast for EU nations, only Italy and Greece were outside the three percent level, but the Commission added that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio in 1997 could be 3.0 percent if existing and new measures prove effective.

"It is a signal at the European level that Italy is rather weak and that other countries are unwilling to recognise the latest budget measures," said Lorenzo Codogno chief economist at Bank of America in Milan.

Economists pointed out that only Italy and Greece came above the three percent level for 1997, and the Commission's forecasts saw Italy's deficit to GDP ratio in 1998 ballooning to 3.9 percent in 1998.
